Work order complete. Here's the report:

## What changed
Two new files, nothing else touched:

- **`src/mem_mcp/util_text.py`** — new module exposing `slugify_title(title: str) -> str`.
  - `from __future__ import annotations`, full type hints, module + function docstrings.
  - Precompiled module-level regex `_NON_ALNUM_RUN_RE = re.compile(r"[^a-z0-9]+")` — ASCII-only (intentionally not `\W`, which is Unicode-aware), per spec.
  - Pure function: lowercases + trims, collapses every non-`[a-z0-9]` run to a single `-`, then strips edge hyphens. All-punctuation/whitespace/unicode-only input returns `""`. Idempotent by construction.
  - Follows the style of the sibling `memory/normalize.py` (stdlib-only, precompiled regex, constants UPPER_CASE).

- **`tests/unit/test_util_text.py`** — plain pytest, no DB fixtures, no `pg_pool` dependency.
  - `pytest.mark.parametrize` covers every required case: normal text, whitespace trim/collapse, punctuation runs, leading/trailing punctuation, digits kept, empty/whitespace-only/punctuation-only, unicode letters (`Café Déjà Vu` → `caf-d-j-vu`, `日本語` → `""`), and idempotence cases.
  - Plus a dedicated `test_slugify_title_is_idempotent` for belt-and-suspenders coverage.

## Verification
- `pytest tests/unit/test_util_text.py -q` → **14 passed**.
- `ruff check src/mem_mcp/util_text.py tests/unit/test_util_text.py` → **All checks passed!**
- `ruff format --check` on both files → **2 files already formatted**.
- `mypy src/mem_mcp/util_text.py` (project `strict = true`) → **Success: no issues found in 1 source file**.
- `git status` → only the two new untracked files; no existing files modified.

Nothing was left open or uncertain — all acceptance criteria are met.
